prompt: You fly a kite on a straight string $40$ m long. The kite is $20$ m above your hands. What angle does the string make with the level ground, in degrees?
hint: The string is the hypotenuse and the height is opposite the angle, so sine is the tool.

hints.text: The string is the hypotenuse and the height is opposite the angle, so sine is the tool.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: a $10$ m string with the kite $5$ m up gives $\sin(\text{angle}) = \frac{5}{10} = \frac{1}{2}$, so the angle is $30^\circ$. Same move, bigger numbers.
$\sin(\text{angle}) = \frac{20}{40} = \frac{1}{2}$. Now ask which angle has sine $\frac{1}{2}$.

explanation: Label the triangle: string $= $ hypotenuse $= 40$, height $= $ opposite $= 20$.
Inverse sine turns the ratio back into an angle: $30^\circ$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Recognize the half-hypotenuse
steps: The height is exactly half the string.
The only right triangle where a leg is half the hypotenuse is the $30$-$60$-$90$.
The angle across from that short leg is $30^\circ$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Ratio to angle, in that order
steps: Sine takes an angle and gives a ratio; inverse sine goes backward.
Here you already have the ratio $\frac{1}{2}$, so you need the backward trip.
The angle whose sine is $\frac{1}{2}$ is $30^\circ$.
